clue.text: Supports a lot of practical details

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments
stacks of something means a great quantity of it

explanation.surface: Something holds up a great many of the nitty-gritty details of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' looks like a verb but it is a plural noun for undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: To get down to the basics is to get down to these, the essential practical facts of a matter.

clue.text: Evade how one's admitted to restricted event?

definitions.meaning: to go round or avoid something

definitions.text: how one's admitted to restricted event?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, entry ..., the ticket or permit that gets you into a closed event

explanation.definitionFit: To evade an obstacle is to go round it, and an event with restricted entry admits people only by means of a pass.

clue.text: A place for contest — one of many explored by negotiators?

definitions.text: one of many explored by negotiators?

parts.note: a venue is where a match or contest is held

explanation.surface: A setting for a sporting contest is likened to something diplomats investigate at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Negotiators are said to explore every possible route to agreement, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: negotiators explore various avenues, meaning possible approaches or lines of action.

clue.text: Employee's claim with needless fiddling?

indicators.note: fiddling suggests tampering, so the letters of the words before it are reworked

explanation.surface: A worker submits an expense claim and pads it with unnecessary items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges the letters of WITH NEEDLESS; it also hints at fraudulent expenses in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang American term for an expense account claim, especially one inflated by a dishonest employee.

clue.text: TV presenter has one opponent

parts.note: Ant McPartlin, of the British TV presenting duo Ant and Dec
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A television host faces a single rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a proposal is said to be its opposer, a noun use of the word.

clue.text: A top hacker arranged a sharp blow

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An expert computer intruder sets up a devastating strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of A TOP HACKER; the hacker of the surface is a computer criminal, not a chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A martial arts strike delivered with the side of the open hand is a sharp blow.

clue.text: Expression of incredulity disgraced cricketer

definitions.meaning: a scornful retort meaning 'I don't believe that for a moment'
Mohammad ..., the Pakistani fast bowler jailed in the 2010 spot-fixing scandal

explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is a scoffing exclamation of disbelief and also the surname of a banned Pakistani bowler.

clue.text: Cast off wicked diabolical female

parts.note: to shed something is to cast it off, like a snake's skin
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw aside a wicked, devilish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious, spiteful woman is likened to a female fiend.

clue.text: Make slight adjustment to excellent piece of music

parts.note: fine means excellent
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks a superb musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something precisely, by small amounts, for optimum performance.

clue.text: Very old times seeing unfortunate Troy perish

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things going awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient history recounts the ill-fated city of Troy being destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' rearranges the letters of TROY PERISH; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The period before written records counts as very old times indeed.

clue.text: Unproductive old film director

definitions.meaning: barren or meagre, as in a poor year or season
David ..., British director of Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.definitionFit: Lean years are unproductive ones, and David Lean was a celebrated British film director of the last century.

clue.text: Tongue-lashing sending words cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the words are treated harshly, wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sends harsh words in a verbal attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' rearranges the letters of SENDING WORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding or reprimand, a synonym of a verbal lashing.

clue.text: Strongly built den about right

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the study goes around the letter

parts.note: a den is a private study or work room

explanation.surface: A robust cosy room positioned to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: solidly and strongly constructed, robust.

clue.text: Most severe saint with 'important' name

parts.note: Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest puns on the name Ernest

explanation.surface: A saint whose name signals his significance proves the strictest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks point to Wilde's comedy, in which being called Ernest is all-important.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a synonym for severe or harsh.

clue.text: Sobriquet of Labour leader embracing relationship with gusto

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping around, so the nickname surrounds another piece

parts.note: Red Ed was a nickname for Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party
blood means kinship or family relationship

explanation.surface: A Labour leader's nickname is linked to some family connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of vigour and enthusiasm, so doing something lustily or with gusto.

clue.text: Consequence concerned with striking

parts.note: re means about or concerning
percussion is the act of striking one thing against another

explanation.surface: An outcome relating to a strike action.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintended after-effect or consequence of an action, a near synonym.

clue.text: Scene of mutiny using special facilities of mine

parts.note: the pithead is the top of a mine shaft and its surface buildings

explanation.surface: Where a revolt broke out, using particular equipment from a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: SPITHEAD, an anchorage off Portsmouth, was the scene of the 1797 Royal Navy mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the anchorage in the Solent where Royal Navy sailors mutinied in 1797.

clue.text: Bill Black got to confess about knife crime

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the confession word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to sing is underworld slang for confessing to the police
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A man called Bill Black admits to a crime involving a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the containment; 'Bill Black' reads as a person's name, and 'sing' is criminal slang for confessing to police.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack with a knife is one example of knife crime.

clue.text: Man getting expression of disapproval after golfer's last shot can resort to violence

indicators.note: after places the man and the jeer following the golf stroke

parts.note: a putt is the final stroke that sinks the ball on each hole
he is the male pronoun
boo is a jeer
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A golfer misses the final putt, a man boos, and someone may lash out.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to kick someone when down, or attack ferociously, is to resort to violence.

clue.text: River in New England state on the sea

indicators.note: in places the river letter within the state name

parts.note: Maine is a New England state in the US

explanation.surface: A river in a north-eastern US state flows to the ocean.

clue.text: Fortification left surrounded by group of Indians

indicators.note: surrounded by means the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class in Indian society

explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a large fortified building, an example of a fortification.

clue.text: Head of board taking pill before work

indicators.note: before places the pill ahead of the work in the answer

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A company chairman pops a pill before getting down to business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of board' looks like a chairman; the board is a table, and its head is its upper surface.

clue.text: Lizard found in Antigua, naturally

indicators.note: found in means the answer is sitting within the following words

explanation.surface: A lizard occurs on the Caribbean island of Antigua in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' shows the letters run across the end of Antigua and the start of naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical American lizard, so an example of a lizard.

clue.text: Catastrophe — atmosphere needs lifting

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means raising the letters up, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mood is an atmosphere, as in the mood of a meeting

clue.text: Very long European film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A lengthy European movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something huge or lengthy, as in an epic journey.

clue.text: I upset goodliest visionary

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of I and GOODLIEST.

clue.text: Enjoys accommodation

definitions.meaning: slang: likes or appreciates, as in 'he really likes jazz'
informal British term for rented rooms or lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for likes, and also British informal for lodgings, especially a student's rented room.

clue.text: Nevada made corrupt couple first to sin

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged
